subject: Request: Chair-level review — Liability rewrite + 35% pilot discount for Meridian Health
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@meridianhealth.com>, procurement@meridianhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood SOW & commercial — pilot proposal and redlines attached

Alex / procurement team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is SOW v3 with the redlines your legal team requested highlighted and our initial commercial worksheet. Key points for the 90-day pilot:

- Pilot scope: 3 clinical workflows, up to 75 concurrent users.
- Proposed pilot price: $85,000 (one-time) with a one-time services fee; licensing at list would have been $115,000.
- Commercial ask: we proposed a 26% pilot concession to get you into production quickly — details in pricing-sheet.xlsx.

A couple of things flagged on the contract redlines: your team requested a removal of Redwood’s cap on indirect damages and a broad carveout to our indemnity for third-party claims. Those are high-risk items for us.

If Meridian needs modifications to liability/indemnity that deviate from our standard risk profile, I’ll need to route for senior review. If you can share the specific sections you want changed and the commercial trade (e.g., higher discount or extended proof-of-concept), we can evaluate and get it to the right approver.

Attached: Meridian_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf, pricing-sheet.xlsx

Next steps: Please confirm whether Meridian is prepared to accept our standard insurance/indemnity language or is seeking the broader protections shown in the redlines. If you are requesting both a liability expansion and a deeper price concession, we’ll need exec signoff.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call this afternoon if helpful.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0142

From: Meridian Legal <legal@meridianhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Porter <aporter@meridianhealth.com>, procurement@meridianhealth.com
Date: 2028-05-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SOW & commercial — pilot proposal and redlines attached

Jasmine —

Thanks for the materials. Meridian's legal review flagged two items that are non-negotiable for our risk/compliance board:

1) Liability cap: Meridian requires a firm cap of $10,000,000 aggregate for the pilot and subsequent contract term. We cannot accept the lower caps in your standard form.

2) Indemnity: Please remove the carveback related to data claims and expand indemnity to cover third-party suits arising out of alleged PHI exposure resulting from Redwood’s services.

From a commercial perspective, our procurement team will only accept those changes if Redwood can provide a deeper concession: we require a 35% pilot discount off list to sign the pilot SOW within two weeks.

If Redwood is unable to accommodate, we will be forced to pause the pilot. Please advise who at Redwood can authorize these changes so we can move to signature.

Regards,
M. Legal
Meridian Health Legal Counsel
legal@meridianhealth.com

To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-05-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Meridian legal — liability bump to $10M + 35% discount request (needs chair-level review)

Team —

Forwarding Meridian’s reply. They want liability increased to $10M and indemnity broadened to include PHI third-party claims. Procurement is conditioning the request on a 35% concession for the pilot.

Why I’m escalating:
- The indemnity change removes our carvebacks around customer-initiated data claims and is precedent-setting for healthcare customers.
- $10M cap materially increases our maximum exposure for this account (pilot + production).
- The commercial ask (35% pilot discount) is ~9 points beyond our typical pilot concessions for comparable customers and would push the deal economics below our target CAC payback.

What I recommend:
1) Consider a counter: 25% pilot discount + limited liability cap at $5M aggregate for the pilot (with insurance requirement of $5M per occurrence / $10M aggregate).
2) Maintain indemnity limited to willful misconduct/gross negligence and carve out downstream customer-to-third-party IP/PHI claims unless directly caused by Redwood’s gross negligence.
3) Require a mutual SOC 2 attestation and evidence of cyber insurance as a condition to any expanded cap.

Requesting a decision path: Marissa / Laura — can you weigh in whether finance/legal can accept the $5M/25% compromise? If not, does this require CEO or Chair signoff? Rishi / Ben — if approved, I’ll draft SOW v4 and updated pricing for signature.

Appended: Meridian_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf

Thanks —
Jasmine

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Meridian legal — liability bump to $10M + 35% discount request (needs chair-level review)

Jasmine —

Thanks for pulling this together and for the thoughtful counter-proposal. I’ve reviewed the redlines and the suggested compromise. My position: we should not accept a $10M aggregate cap for the pilot without substantial commercial protection. However, I will approve escalation to authorize a limited one-time concession on commercial and liability under the following strict conditions: 

1) Pricing: authorize up to a 25% pilot discount only. Anything beyond 25% requires CEO signoff.
2) Liability: authorize a pilot aggregate cap of $5,000,000 (five million) provided Meridian furnishes:
   - Evidence of cyber liability insurance with at least $5M per occurrence / $10M aggregate, and
   - Proof of SOC 2 Type II within the last 12 months, and
   - A 12-month aggregation window for the cap tied only to fees paid under the pilot and first year of paid production.
3) Indemnity language: we will not broaden indemnity to cover PHI-related third-party claims absent a factual showing that Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct caused the event. We must preserve the carvebacks for customer-provided data and downstream claims.
4) Precedent: include clear contractual language that this concession is limited to Meridian’s pilot and is not to be used as precedent in any future contracting discussions without express finance/legal approval.

If Meridian counters accepting these conditions, Laura — please prepare a redlined SOW v4 that incorporates the $5M cap, the insurance/SOC 2 conditions, and the indemnity limit. Ben / Rishi — proceed with updated pricing reflecting the 25% pilot discount.

I’m comfortable approving this path without CEO signoff as long as Meridian agrees to the insurance/SOC2 requirements and the precedent clause. If Meridian insists on $10M or 35% discount, escalate to CEO.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@meridianhealth.com>, procurement@meridianhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-31T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SOW & commercial — pilot proposal (counter proposal enclosed)

Alex / procurement —

Appreciate the clear asks from your legal team. Meridian’s request to expand the liability cap to $10M and broaden indemnity triggered an internal review. We want to move forward and support a fast pilot, so Redwood can offer the following counter if Meridian will accept the conditions below: 

Counter-offer (pilot):
- Pilot price: list $115,000 with a negotiated 25% one-time concession = $86,250.
- Liability cap: $5,000,000 aggregate for the pilot and first 12 months of paid production, contingent on:
   • Meridian providing cyber liability insurance with a minimum $5M per occurrence / $10M aggregate, and
   • Evidence of SOC 2 Type II within past 12 months.
- Indemnity: Redwood will accept indemnity for third-party claims only to the extent such claims are caused by Redwood’s willful misconduct or gross negligence. We are not able to accept a broad PHI indemnity absent a showing of Redwood’s direct culpability.
- Precedent clause: This commercial and liability treatment is limited to Meridian’s pilot and is not precedent for other contracts.

Attached is SOW v4 reflecting the updated cap and the insurance/SOC 2 condition: Meridian_SOW_v4_final_for_signature.pdf

If Meridian accepts, please countersign the attached DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/shared/meridian-deal-47 and we will schedule kickoff. If you prefer a 1:1 call to walk through the conditions, I’m available tomorrow morning.

Best regards,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
